args.summary: After the latest deploy, checkout-api v2.3.1 was running in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and failing health checks, with an error rate of 18%. Deploy history shows v2.3.1-rc (seq 2) and v2.3.1 (seq 3) were both unhealthy. The most recent healthy release is v2.3.0 (seq 1). I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all production regions. After the rollback the service is healthy in all three regions and the error rate is 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression before redeploying.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened the SEV2 incident.

**Rollback:**
- v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an 18% error rate.
- v2.3.0 is the most recent healthy release. The release candidate deployed just before v2.3.1 (v2.3.1-rc) had also been unhealthy, so I skipped it.
- After the rollback, all three regions are on v2.3.0 and healthy, with a 0.2% error rate.

**Incident:**
- **INC-0002** (SEV2, checkout-api) is open and on-call has been paged. It describes the failure, the rollback to v2.3.0, the recovery, and the next step: finding the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying.
- My first attempt to create the incident timed out. Before trying again, I checked the incident list: it was empty, so the second attempt shouldn't have created a duplicate. The ID INC-0002 suggests an INC-0001 may exist somewhere. It wasn't in the list, but it's worth a quick check that on-call wasn't paged twice.
